page: Amazon Web Services r5d.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It operates on an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, delivering 16 virtual CPUs across 8 dedicated physical cores with two threads per core. The instance configuration features 128 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a dedicated 600 GB local NVMe SSD instance storage volume and a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. Accelerated graphics hardware is not present.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across multi-threaded and memory-bound operations, supported by uncached read bandwidth of 86.72 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 45.72 GB/sec. Synthetic database metrics achieve 5,403.07 PassMark database operations, while Redis SET throughput reaches 13.19 million operations per second. Multi-threaded processing reaches 6,555 points in Geekbench and 13,523.06 in multi-core stress-ng. However, single-core processing capabilities fall into lower percentiles, as observed in single-thread stress-ng scores of 1,284.08 and single-core Geekbench ratings of 1,036.0, alongside slower bzip3 decompression rates.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of 600 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD storage eliminates the immediate need for external block storage when running temporary caching tiers or high-IOPS scratch disks. While per-core single-threaded compute throughput shows its generation limits compared to compute-centric instances, the high memory density per core delivers efficient resource utilization for memory-bound systems. Workload fit includes in-memory databases such as Redis and Memcached, relational databases handling caching or staging tables, data transformation pipelines, and mid-sized search indexing engines.
description: Amazon Web Services r5d.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor operating at 3.1 GHz. The platform provides 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores), 128 GB of DDR4 memory, and 600 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD instance storage without integrated GPUs. Network bandwidth sits at a 5 Gbps baseline. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves average-tier multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth, reaching 13.19 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 86.72 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations. Single-threaded metrics, including compression and single-core stress tests, reflect lower relative performance. The combination of an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and high-speed local NVMe storage provides practical utility for caching services, relational databases, distributed memory stores, and batch data processing where high random I/O and large working memory sets are primary constraints.
